paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Polarity scores for Japan
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the frequency counts of polarity scores for Japan. The x-axis is labeled "Polarity scores" and uses a linear scale with tick marks ranging from -1.0 to 0.6 at intervals of 0.2, with the plotted data extending from approximately -1.1 to 0.55. No units are provided for the x-axis. The y-axis is labeled "Counts" and utilizes a linear scale ranging from 0 to slightly above 40000, with tick marks evenly spaced at intervals of 10000. The data is represented by a single solid blue line featuring solid circular markers. The line begins at an x-value of roughly -1.1 with a y-value near 0 and remains relatively steady near 0 until x ≈ -0.65. It then rises to a minor peak of approximately 5000 at x ≈ -0.55, dips to roughly 2500 at x ≈ -0.35, and subsequently increases sharply to reach its highest peak of approximately 41500 at x = 0.0. Following this primary peak, the line experiences a series of sharp fluctuations: it declines steeply to a value of about 8500 at x ≈ 0.1, rebounds to a secondary peak of approximately 26500 at x ≈ 0.18, falls dramatically to roughly 1000 at x ≈ 0.35, and rises again to a tertiary peak of about 13000 at x ≈ 0.45. The line ultimately concludes near a count of 0 at the end of the x-axis (x ≈ 0.55).
